description: A link (http or https), a title, and an optional description; who added it ('You' for your own); the prototype's free-text 'where to find it' and optional Backs up & Limits dropped (the builder, Nov 14–15); Undo.
tier_why: Credibility judgments need inspectable evidence.
design_gaps: Built on the server (M1-8) and on the card (M1-9); the first example board carries the prototype's sources. Reworked with the builder (Nov 14–15), after Google Docs' Insert link and Wikipedia's citation tool: the form asks for a Link first (with a link icon; http or https only, up to 2,000 characters, since there are no uploads yet), then a Title, then an optional Description, each with an example; Backs up and Limits dropped (the description can say them), and who added a source is shown instead; the columns stay. Reset warnings say the credibility score resets. As in the prototype, anyone who can contribute adds a source to a wording; only the person who added it edits it. Taking a source off a wording is for whoever added it, the wording's author, or the Owner (the builder, Nov 14; the Editor takes the Owner's place when M2 adds it). One source can back several wordings: a source already on the board can be cited on another. Taking a source off a wording leaves it on the board, since nothing is removed from a board. Remove takes it off at once with a ten-second Undo, held in the browser as a deleted wording is, in place of the prototype's second click (the builder, Nov 15). Where to find it stays text, and is a link only when it is an http or https address. Not designed: a way to pick a source already on the board, which the prototype doesn't have.

In the app (M1-9): the source form warns that the credibility score resets ("Credibility scores reset on N wordings" for a shared source), and Remove needed a second click. Since Nov 15, Remove takes the source off at once, its Undo bar saying "Source removed. The credibility score resets." Not yet: the note saying why the meter is unreviewed after a reset.

design_gaps: Built in the app (M1-5, M2-1): the server checks all five roles, Viewer, Voter, Contributor, Editor, and Owner, on every read and write (one policy table, can(), and the matrix test for all seven personas). Decided Nov 17: no header line saying what you can do (Google Docs and Figma have none; the faded controls say it). Not yet: a way to make someone an Editor outside the tests (the people list, M2-2b); a way to ask for more access (none in M2). Since Nov 17, the reason also shows on hover (the hint box).

description: Address for every board (#b=), version (&v=), and comment (&c=); the address follows what's open; Back/Forward and reload work. Copy link on versions and comments. Opening a link reveals and rings its target; deleted version/comment and unknown board have their own states; signed-out links to non-public boards sign in first without showing the question.
tier_why: Collaborators arrive through links; every board needs a stable URL. Card-level links can follow (T3).
complexity_why: Router + stable ids that survive combine/separate.
design_gaps: Built in the app (M1-7), as paths rather than the prototype's #b=…&v=…: /b/<board> and /b/<board>/v/<version>, so Google sign-in comes back to the very version. The address follows the version opened by its wording, changing in place, so Back leaves the board; reload, Back, and Forward work. Copy link in a version's ⋯ menu. A version's link shows its column, unfolds its row unless it leads it, and opens and rings it; a deleted or unknown version opens the board with "That version was deleted." and Dismiss; a board that doesn't exist says so and leads to New steelman (M1 has no list of boards). Signed out, a board's link asks to sign in first and shows nothing. Not yet: comment links (D-01). Link previews (title and image when pasted into chat apps) not designed. 'No access' for signed-in people waits on Request access (H-04).

description: Real: first-visit analytics notice (OK / Turn off), Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track honored, privacy page, analytics switch in Account, Download your data (JSON). Delete account (type username; writing stays, credited to deleted_account): simulated in the prototype, real in the app since M1-12.
tier_why: US-standard notice and opt-out for analytics and replays, plus export and deletion, before real users arrive.
complexity_why: Server-side export and deletion jobs; anonymizing authorship while keeping boards intact; consent stored per account as well as per browser.
design_gaps: In the app (M1-12): Your account shows username, email, and sign-in methods, with Download your data and Delete account, run as architecture §2's table (the builder's decisions, Nov 15: a board with no editor or contributor left is deleted; the username is held 30 days; PostHog isn't asked, as analytics are anonymous). In the app (M1-13, a draft for the builder): a privacy page at /privacy with architecture §7's eight points, readable signed out, with the analytics switch, linked from the notice and Your account; a Content Security Policy on every answer. Left: a qualified review of the page before public communities; the daily call that releases held usernames (M1-14); Sign out and the analytics switch aren't on the page yet; on a phone, the account button steps aside on a board, as in the prototype.
